t: A Basque kingdom of the western Pyrenees, ruled from Pamplona, which emerged around 824 between the Franks and the Muslim Ebro valley.
Under Sancho III the Great (1004–1035) it dominated Christian Iberia, and his sons founded the royal lines of Castile and Aragon.
Castile conquered its southern part in 1512, but Navarre kept its own laws until 1841, while its northern kings became kings of France.
dyk: In 958 the elderly Queen Toda of Pamplona travelled to Córdoba with her grandson Sancho the Fat of León, who was treated there by the caliph’s physician for his obesity.
ev: Íñigo Arista becomes ruler of Pamplona after a Frankish defeat at Roncevaux
Sancho Garcés I founds the Jimena dynasty
Sancho III the Great occupies León, the height of his power
Murder of Sancho IV at Peñalén; Pamplona passes to the king of Aragon
García Ramírez restores an independent kingdom
Sancho VII fights at Las Navas de Tolosa
Ferdinand the Catholic conquers Upper Navarre
The Ley Paccionada makes Navarre a province of Spain

f.successor: Crown of Castile (Upper Navarre); Kingdom of France (Lower Navarre); Spanish province of Navarre (1841)
